To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Senior Psychology majors who have served as URCA Assistats are more knowledgeable about statistics, critical thinking, and writing than their peers who have not served as Assistants.

Students who had participated as URCA Assistant were significantly more likely to be female, Caucasian, and have higher grade point average, but were not different from those who had no URCA experience in terms of age, class standing, or self rated knowledge of statistics or technology.
URCA Assistants are more likely to be female, have a higher GPA, and have more experience in research than non Assistants.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: 1) Are students who serve as URCA Assistant distinguishable from those that do not in terms of their scores on the Senior Exit Exam?
the following questions: 1) Are URCA students more successful on the exit exam, in terms of overall score?
the following: 1. Does participation in the URAC program predict knowledge of psychology?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the URCA program provides an excellent opportunity for students to learn and practice skills that are necessary in the field of Psychology, and that students who participate in URCA tend to have higher scores on the Senior Exit Exam, and thus may be better prepared for the job market or graduate school.
the URCA program has no effect on the knowledge, skills or abilities of Psychology students at our university.

URCA Assistants have more knowledge of psychology, better critical thinking skills, and better technology skills than non Assistants; however, this difference is small and is not statistically significant.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Exit Exam has been shown to be reliable (Cronbach's alpha =.91) and valid (as evidenced by the fact that students who score higher on the exam have better GPAs than those who score lower) (see http: //www.psychology.unl.edu/undergrad/exitexam.html for more information).
the Senior Exit Exam is a valid measure of knowledge of psychology, statistics and methods, and critical thinking in psychology, but not necessarily of career knowledge or writing skills.
the Senior Exit Exam is an assessment of the knowledge gained in our Psychology courses and the skills necessary for success in our field.
The main takeaway from our work is that
URCA Assistants are distinguishable in terms of knowledge, critical thinking skills, and writing skills from their counterparts who did not serve as URCA Assist ants.
URCA Assistant participation does not appear to have a significant impact on the knowledge, skills, and abilities measured by the Senior Exit Exam.
students who participate in URCA are more likely to be female, have higher grades, and be older than those who do not participate in URCA.
